name: Compote of Chestnuts
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Remove husks and skin from the chestnuts
Boil gently in the milk and water until like floury potatoes, and strain them
Boil the sugar until it purls on the surface and flavor with vanilla bean
Add the chestnuts and work all together vigorously
Rub through a potato masher on to a dish
Pile up whipped cream in the centre of a dish
Gently strew the chestnuts on top of the cream in a conical form
Garnish with orange quarters soaked in maraschino at the base of the cream and nuts

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Remove husks and skin from the chestnuts
2. Boil gently in the milk and water until like floury potatoes, and strain them
3. Boil the sugar until it purls on the surface and flavor with vanilla bean
4. Add the chestnuts and work all together vigorously
5. Rub through a potato masher on to a dish
6. Pile up whipped cream in the centre of a dish
7. Gently strew the chestnuts on top of the cream in a conical form
8. Garnish with orange quarters soaked in maraschino at the base of the cream and nuts
